name: Zane Lowell
reason: The protagonist's Chinese name Luo Zheng was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Zane' was chosen as a strong, modern name for the lead; the surname 'Lowell' was assigned to his family (source Luo Clan) to create a consistent family unit with his sister Elara Lowell (Luo Yan).
description: The protagonist of the show, present in every episode from 1 to 1321. Once the prodigy heir of House Lowell, Zane was branded a traitor's son after his family's fall and reduced to a slave, forced into shackles and sent to the Lowell Training Hall (Ep 1). From that lowest point he claws his way back, joining the Skyreach Sect and rising through the cultivation ranks, reaching half a step into the Nature Level by Ep 114 and continuing through the Adept and Soul Realms and far beyond. His journey carries him from the Eastern Territory to the Heartlands and eventually to higher worlds, driven by the need to free and protect his sister Elara. Aided by the Cobalt Dragon entity in his mind, he becomes a master cultivator, forger, and the central figure of every major arc, making lifelong enemies such as Maddox and allies such as Tia and Lavender along the way.

name: Zane Jones
reason: Source pseudonym 'Luo Tianxing' (the alias Luo Zheng uses in the Black Jade Martial House arc) was localized as 'Zane Jones' - keeping the hero's first name and adding a deliberately common surname so it works as an unremarkable cover identity.
description: The pseudonym Zane Lowell uses in the Divine Kingdom arcs (Eps ~784-1265). Introduced as 'a warrior of the Harlen Divine Kingdom' who 'fights out of the Black Jade Martial House' (Ep 809), it corresponds to the source pseudonym Luo Tianxing that Luo Zheng adopts in the same chapters. It is an intentional in-story alias of the protagonist, not a separate character.

name: Zane Finn and Lewis

name: Vitality
reason: The source cultivation energy 'Zhen Yuan' (True Essence) was localized as 'Vitality'; this is the show's canonical term for the energy, replacing the abandoned draft term 'Aether' (the separate item 'Aether Crystal' is unaffected).
description: The fundamental cultivation energy wielded by cultivators from the Adept Stage upward; below that stage warriors cannot even use Vitality for protection (Ep 151). It is shaped into shields strong enough to stop Demon Commanders (Ep 126), tendrils, whips and full constructs such as a giant hawk of pure Vitality (Ep 154), and can be stolen or scattered by a sufficiently skilled fighter (Eps 124, 152). Episode contexts map directly onto the source's Zhen Yuan scenes, e.g. Zane scattering an opponent's gathered Vitality mirrors Luo Zheng kicking apart a foe's condensed Zhen Yuan. Related canonical terms include Shadow Vitality (Zane's shadow-element manipulation, NOT 'Shadow Aether') and Supreme Vitality crystals, the Heartlands currency of pure unbonded Vitality distinct from Aether Crystals and Crystal Cubes.

name: Cloud Hall
reason: The source organization name 'Cloud Hall' was retained unchanged, as the English term already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: A powerful cultivation organization that stands above the Skyreach Sect in the world's hierarchy (Eps 189-270). Admission is won by conquering the Cloud Road trial, and being chosen as a Cloud Hall disciple - especially a 'core disciple', a rank unique to Cloud Hall - confers status above even a sect leader (Ep 227). The Skyreach Sect's strength rests partly on Cloud Hall's backing, and earning Cloud Hall's favor is treated as a license to act with near impunity in the Eastern Territory. It maps one-to-one to the source's Cloud Hall (chapters 32-1304), whose Palace Master is Ning Yudie (localized as Tia).

name: Tia
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a short Western feminine name. 'Tia' covers both of the source character's identities - the alias 'Xiao Die' under which she first appears and her true name Ning Yudie - collapsing them into one consistent localized name given to her in-show by the Cobalt Dragon (Ep 391).
description: A major supporting heroine introduced around Ep 390 as a Cloud Hall disciple disguised as a male; she is revealed to be a powerful, beautiful woman and is named by the Cobalt Dragon in Ep 391. She carries a sky-blue gem that summons an Ice Phoenix - matching the source's Xiao Die, who summons an Ice Phoenix from her Jade Treasure in the Cloud Road chapters - and she hunts the Crystal Key to the fallen Sixth-Tier Sect's treasures alongside Zane (Eps 391-392). Her stated first-grade Soul Realm cultivation badly understates her real power: in the source she is Ning Yudie, the Palace Master of the Cloud Hall, a Void Tribulation powerhouse who dispersed her cultivation nine times to rebuild it without bottlenecks. Cunning and fierce, she remains one of Zane's most important allies through the end of the show (Eps 391-1320).

name: Heartland
reason: The source region 'Central Domain' was renamed 'the Heartlands' to fit the Western fantasy register while preserving the sense of a continent's central heartland region.
description: The vast central region of the world, dwarfing the Eastern Territory roughly tenfold in size (Ep 294) and home to the world's true powers. The Seven Great Houses that dominate the Eastern Territory 'would be laughed out of The Heartlands' (Ep 296), and its clans, lords and sects - including Maddox, the mysterious lord behind the Soul Harvesting Ritual (Ep 309) - operate on a different scale entirely. Reaching the Heartlands to measure himself against the wider world becomes one of Zane's defining mid-story goals (Ep 352), and the region remains the stage for most arcs from roughly Ep 352 onward. It maps to the source's Central Domain (chapters 245-1304). Episodes overwhelmingly use the plural form 'Heartlands' (279 mentions vs 2 singular).

name: Soul Sea Realm
reason: The source cultivation stage 'Divine Sea Realm' was renamed 'Soul Sea Realm', keeping the show's 'Soul'-based realm naming scheme consistent (Soul Realm, Soul Sea Realm).
description: A high cultivation realm appearing from Ep 510 through the end of the show, far above the Soul Realm. Breaking through to it is a major milestone - below the Soul Sea Realm cultivation depends on pure talent (Ep 1115) - and it has early and late stages plus numbered levels (e.g. 'fourth-level', 'late-stage'). Even a freshly broken-through Soul Sea Realm warrior cannot fight a whole city (Ep 1117), but a handful of them constitutes a serious armed force. Its episode range (510-1320) aligns precisely with the source's Divine Sea Realm (chapters 497-1308), and aligned scenes such as Zane 'barely crossing into' it (Ep 1118) match Luo Zheng having 'just stepped into the Divine Sea Realm' in the corresponding chapters. Note the source's separate 'Spirit Sea Realm' is a different, higher concept and should not be conflated.

name: Ogre
issues: Possible split terminology: the source's single Demon Race is rendered as 'Ogre' in most arcs (the two-hearted creature of Eps 47-48 is the source's two-hearted Demon of ch 32), but the early war arc (Eps ~105-130) keeps 'Demon General'/'Demon Commanders' for the same race's officers. Verify whether the show intends Ogres and war-arc Demons as one race or two.
description: The show's name for the source novel's Demon Race, the monstrous horned race that serves as humanity's primary racial enemy (Eps 28-1296). Ogres are hulking, fast and tough - the one Zane fights in Eps 47-48 has horns sprouting from its skull and a hidden second heart on its back that must be pierced to kill it, exactly matching the source's two-hearted Demons. They field a military hierarchy of Governors, War Lords, War Sages and Saint Lords, besiege the Tower of Sin region in the mid-show arcs, and are named alongside humans and the Demon Night as one of the world's major races (Ep 1123). The source renders the same race variously as Demon Race, Devil Race and Demon Clan.

name: Ogre War Lord
reason: The source rank 'War Venerable' (also rendered 'War Reverend') held by Demon Race powerhouses was localized as 'War Lord' for the Ogres, a clearer Western fantasy military title.
description: A senior Ogre military rank appearing in Eps 564-945, above the Ogre Governor and below the Ogre War Sage. A single Ogre War Lord is treated as the strongest thing on a battlefield and more than a match for Zane at the time (Eps 565-566); the scene of one War Lord being joined by two more matches the source's three Devil/Demon War Venerables pursuing Luo Zheng in chapter 551. At least one, Don, is individually named (Ep 580). The Demon Night race uses the same 'War Lord' rank term (Ep 611).

name: Ogre War Sage
reason: The source rank 'Battle Saint' (the Life and Death Realm tier) was localized as 'War Sage' for Ogre powerhouses, matching the show's War Lord / War Sage ladder.
description: An elite Ogre rank above War Lord, appearing in Eps 611-945 with graded levels (e.g. 'fourth-level Ogre War Sage', Ep 941). The two War Sages Colin and Neil whose arrival 'changed everything' and who smashed the two great gates (Eps 612-618) correspond directly to the source's Demon Race Battle Saints who smashed the Sin Tower's entrance doors in the aligned chapters (553-923).

name: Ogre Governor
reason: An Ogre officer rank below War Lord; the aligned source chapters (~550-552) feature a 'demon commander' that Luo Zheng fights, which is the most plausible counterpart, though the source's 'War General' rank is also a candidate.
description: An Ogre officer rank appearing in Eps 561-563, used as a power yardstick: most of an approaching Ogre force is 'on par with the Ogre Governor he'd fought before', while the two standout figures are War Lords (Ep 563). It sits at the bottom of the Ogre command ladder beneath War Lord, War Sage and Saint Lord.

name: Ogre Horde
reason: A named move of Zane's early fist technique (the localized form of the source's Heavenly Fiend Fist / Heavenly Demon God Fist); the aligned source chapters describe the technique but give the move no distinct name, so 'Ogre Horde' appears to be an adaptation-side coinage.
description: The second move of Zane's fist technique, learned alongside the first move Earthshatter around Ep 105. Less powerful than Earthshatter but able to strike multiple targets at once, it serves as Zane's crowd-control attack and matures into launching multiple phantom strikes - six Ogre Horde phantoms at once by Ep 387.

name: Ogre Saint Lord
reason: The source rank 'Holy Lord' (as in the Demon Clan Holy Lord of the aligned chapters) was localized as 'Saint Lord', the pinnacle of the Ogre hierarchy above War Sage.
description: The highest Ogre rank shown, appearing in Eps 1140-1145 where the Ogre Saint Lord is one of three Saint Lords monitoring Zane in the abyss through surveillance arrays. This matches the source's Demon Clan Holy Lord observing every movement in the abyss and testing Luo Zheng's strength in the aligned chapters (~1120s).

name: Maddox
reason: The antagonist's Chinese name Cui Xie was fully localized to 'Maddox', a hard-edged Western name chosen to fit a ruthless arch-villain archetype.
description: The show's major mid-to-late antagonist (Eps 351-1179) and Zane's defining nemesis - even near the end, Zane reflects he never wanted to kill anyone as badly 'not even his old nemesis, Maddox' (Ep 1179). An independent cultivator reputed to be the strongest in the Heartlands and 'on a whole other level' (Ep 408), he seeks to complete the Soul Harvesting Ritual and holds Zane's sister Elara captive as one of its required components. He maps to the source's Cui Xie (chapters 338-1159), who likewise pursues the Heavenly Devil Joyous Union Formation requiring three Divine Core women with the Extreme Violet Yin Body - Luo Yan (Elara) among them - making the episode-source correspondence airtight in both role and chapter range. He competes for the Immortals' inheritance around Ep 551 and remains a looming threat across hundreds of episodes.

name: Maddox Zane
reason: Extraction artifact spanning a sentence/clause boundary ('...Maddox. Zane...' / '...Maddox, Zane...'); Maddox and Zane are separate characters.

name: Lavender
reason: The source character's single-syllable Chinese name 'Xun' was localized as 'Lavender', an evocative feminine name suiting a mysterious exiled queen.
description: A major female ally of Zane from Ep 608 through the finale (Eps 608-1321). She is a deposed queen whom Zane has promised to help reclaim her throne (Eps 1114, 1126), and her power base lies with the devout, holy-tree-dwelling Demon Night of the Dark World (Eps 1125-1126). She can speak directly into Zane's mind (Ep 1124), reflecting her source identity: Xun, the woman hidden within Luo Zheng's sword spirit, to whom Luo Zheng likewise promises to help 'return to her throne' in the aligned chapters (~1095+). Cunning and politically ruthless, she once used Zane's Roaring Tokens to broadcast their staged argument to the whole city (Ep 1128), and her throne-reclamation campaign drives the late Dark World arc.

name: Demon Night
reason: The source race 'Demon Night Clan' kept its name, shortened to 'the Demon Night'; the source translation also renders the same clan as 'Yao Ye Clan' and 'Yao Night Clan', all unified under this one localized term.
description: A non-human race introduced in Eps 299-300 (described by the Cobalt Dragon) and prominent through the end of the show. Demon Night individuals are elegant and dangerous, with long slender legs and an aura of Malice (Ep 314), and are counted with humans and Ogres among the world's major races (Ep 1123). They are deeply devout (Ep 1125) and live on and around their holy tree - in the Dark World's northern district their quarter is a massive forest they navigate from birth (Ep 1126). Lavender's claim to a throne runs through this race, mirroring the source where Xun and the Demon Night Clan's royal politics (including the King of Slaughter's lost throne) dominate the late chapters. Maps to the source's Demon Night Clan (chapters 287-1295), also translated there as Yao Ye Clan / Yao Night Clan.

name: Skyreach Sect
reason: The source sect 'Blue Cloud Sect' (also rendered 'Azure Cloud Sect') was renamed 'Skyreach Sect', an aspirational English coinage fitting the Western fantasy register.
description: The main martial sect of the show's first several hundred episodes (Eps 2-1130) and the Eastern Territory's premier cultivation institution; getting into it is young Zane's first great goal (Ep 11). New pledges wear standard white robes (Ep 104), students train at the Sentinel Peaks and run military missions against enemy scouts (Ep 110), and disciples progress from outer to inner to personal disciple ranks, with the sect-wide Skyreach Sect List ranking them all. The sect's power rests both on its leadership and on backing from the higher organization Cloud Hall (Ep 227). It maps to the source's Blue Cloud Sect (chapters 1-1110), with its 33 peaks and Peak Competition.

name: Skyreach Sect List
issues: Name drift: the same disciple ranking is called 'Skyreach Sect Rankings' in Eps 235 and 316 but 'Skyreach Sect List' elsewhere (Eps 259-318); 'List' is the dominant delivered form.
reason: The source sect's disciple ranking board, the 'Azure Sky Proclamation', was localized as the plainer 'Skyreach Sect List' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: The sect-wide ranking of all Skyreach Sect disciples. Anyone in the top hundred is a force to be reckoned with; Adrian ranked fifteenth, Patrick second, and the legendary Evan first, while rankings for personal disciples are considered notoriously unreliable since they rarely fight in public (Eps 259-318). Final rankings are announced by an elder after the sect competition.

name: Skyreach Sect's Bloody Mountain
issues: This is a possessive surface variant; the standalone entity 'Bloody Mountain' (Eps 38-44, 223, 244, 261, 358, including an episode titled 'Bloody Mountain') is the primary form and these 2 mentions should be folded into it if it appears in another batch.
reason: The source trial site 'Bloody Mountain' (also rendered 'Blood Mountain' / 'Red Mountain' in chapters 25-35) kept its name directly in the adaptation.
description: The Skyreach Sect's trial mountain, climbed by Great House disciples and a thousand ordinary candidates during the entrance trial (Eps ~38-44). The higher-ups used Crimson Powder to turn the whole mountain into one giant Runic Circle for trials, and candidates who fail are teleported off it in motes of light.

name: Skyreach Sect Rankings
issues: Name drift: Eps 235 and 316 use 'Skyreach Sect Rankings' for the ranking the other episodes call the 'Skyreach Sect List'.

name: Skyreach Sect Outer Disciple
reason: Generic rank phrase (sect name + the common 'outer disciple' rank), not a distinct entity; the sect itself is already tracked as Skyreach Sect.

name: Skyreach Sect Zane

name: Soul Realm
reason: The source cultivation stage 'Divine Reflection Realm' (also rendered 'Illuminating God realm') was renamed 'Soul Realm', anchoring the show's soul-themed realm naming (Soul Realm, Soul Sea Realm).
description: The cultivation realm directly above the Adept Realm, introduced around Ep 90 as the highest stage then known in the Eastern Territory. A Soul Realm master is a near-mythical figure early on - no one at a Great House can stand up to one (Ep 128), their attacks can obliterate anything below the realm in a heartbeat (Ep 117), and even wealthy families who can hire Adept bodyguards cannot dream of hiring one (Ep 195). Its episode range (90-1186) tracks the source's Divine Reflection Realm (chapters 77-1092), and both sit at the same rung: above Adept/Xiantian, below the Divine Core-equivalent tiers. Note the masterls 'Fighting Soul Realm' (Eps 470, 478) is a separate soul-level concept, not this cultivation realm.

name: Adept Realm
issues: Early name drift: Eps 151-169 call this stage the 'Adept Stage' before the episodes settle on 'Adept Realm' from Ep ~171 onward.
reason: The source cultivation stage 'Xiantian' (the realm above body refining) was localized as the 'Adept Realm', replacing an untranslatable pinyin term with a Western fantasy rank.
description: The cultivation realm above basic body-refining warriors and below the Soul Realm, central to the show's early and middle arcs (Eps 151-1320). It is divided into numbered levels and grades - Initiate Adept at entry, fifth rank, Fourth-Grade, Peak Adept, and the Consummation of the Adept Realm as its ceiling before the Soul Realm. Reaching it is the threshold of real power: Adepts can wield Vitality for protection and attack, and even one makes a formidable bodyguard (Eps 151-195). It corresponds to the source's Xiantian realm (chapters 9-1111), whose 'Xiantian Full Circle' matches the Consummation sub-level.

name: Adept Stage
issues: Early variant: Eps 151-169 use 'Adept Stage' for the stage later episodes consistently call 'Adept Realm'.

name: Adept Realm Zane
reason: Extraction artifact spanning a sentence boundary ('...the Adept Realm. Zane...'); 'Adept Realm' and 'Zane' are separate, already-tracked entities.
